snippet.title: Rocketmen: Axis of Evil (PS3) - Full Playthrough + DLC
snippet.description:
00:00:00 Intro and 1 - Boarded!
00:19:59   2 - To the Rescue
00:42:03   3 - A Daring Escape
01:20:39   4 - Mars Invades!
01:28:38   5 - Ferry Ride
01:40:39   6 - Liberation of Armada
01:57:49   7 - A Sneaky Plan
02:12:29   8 - Caught
02:25:21   9 - The Belly of the Beast
02:46:25 10 - Storming the Castle
03:14:53 11 - Finding Jane
03:37:55 12 - Clear the Asteroids
04:07:37 13 - The Plan

So my friend, Jameson, got a PS3 first. I had (still HAVE, actually) plenty of PS2 games to beat, and saw no real reason to pick up Sony's shiny, new, more powerful game console. That changed when I played Fallout 3. I fell so hard for that game, I picked up a 3 as soon as I could. But between those two times, I was exposed to a variety of PSN titles. When I finally got my 3, I went on a spending spree, picking up many of the games Jameson had either bought or tried the demo for, and Rocketmen was one of them.

So here's the deal. Apparently, the Martian Empire and the Legion of Terra have combined their might and rule the solar system with an iron fist. But the other planets resist these space fascists, along with a group of earth rebels led by Nick Sion and Zach Rathman. You take the role of a Rocketman working closely with Nick, onboard his ship the Icarus Jane. Which means you do everything.

And that's a great name for a ship.
 
It's a stick shooter, and I do enjoy those. At ten levels, with some of them being almost TOO long, you get plenty of bang for your buck. I don't remember exactly, but I think Rocketmen was either 5.99 or 9.99. The former case is an out and out deal, the later is appropriate, and either way, the price matches the content. I'm a huge fan of cell shaded graphics and the cartoony look they give games, and here they go one further by making the cutscenes look like comic panels. Combined with a 50s-future aesthetic and you've got a game that's very easy on the eyes. The voice acting is decent, especially the dude doing a Jim Cummings impression for the Martian, Mash. The music isn't bad, but there's not a whole lot of it. The main theme and the action theme get reused quite a bit, though the DLC has a bit more variety. Speaking of, it adds 3 new levels set on and around Saturn, as well as 3 new special weapons. The dialogue is pretty funny at times, and I'll always appreciate a game where couch co-op is not only an option, but actively makes the game more fun.

On a personal note, I love the Martian gangstas and their low-rider, and I cracked up when the main character has a fit on the last level and refuses to use the consoles any more. I always find it amusing when video game characters get sick and tired of video game logic (Conner from Assassin's Creed III is the undisputed king of this).

Now the bad news. Even though I considered using a new character to give you a SLIGHTLY more accurate look at how hard the game is, Rocketmen: Axis of Evil is not difficult. Some of the levels, as stated above, go on for too damn long (2, 3, and 12). The voice acting, while good, tends to cut off before a character has finished their sentence. I had to complete this in several runs because, despite the nice and interesting environments, the core loop grind DOES get tiresome after awhile. Also, while the story hints at further developments and ends on a cliffhanger on the DLC, with your character and the crew headed for Jupiter, it doesn't go into real detail about, well, anything. Even the last boss, a Darth Vader-esque enforcer for the Legion of Terra named Ivana Folterung, only shows up at the very end of the regular game. And despite being defeated, she doesn't die. I'd kinda like to know how the rebellion goes, overall. Was it worth it, making 2,337,001 Martian children orphans? We'll never know.

So, looking at all that, I'd have to give this one a 6. It's fun and playable for awhile. But you're not going to stop whatever you're doing to run off and play Rocketmen: Axis of Evil. In fact, unless this is on Steam or something, I'm not sure that you CAN play this one, or at least with the DLC. So, I suppose enjoy watching me play through something you'll never do the same with. Sorry about that.

6/10
